name: Ahri
notes: Casts go one at a time: Orb of Deception and Charm each have a 0.25 s cast time (gen.Q.castTimeS, gen.E.castTimeS) during which no other cast starts and no attack lands; Fox-Fire and Spirit Rush have no cast time (the dossier lists 'none') and cost nothing up front, but still wait for a cast already in progress.

Opening: Spirit Rush is cast at t=0 (instant) and recast twice more at the 1 s static interval between casts (its cooldown is 100-140 s so it never becomes available a second time inside a fight this short); Orb of Deception and Charm are cast right after, one after another, each taking its 0.25 s cast time.

Orb of Deception's outbound (magic) and return (true) passes are both resolved at the moment the cast completes: no separate travel time is modeled for a stationary target that sits at the return point.

Fox-Fire's three flames are assumed to land together, at the 0.25 s priority-acquisition delay (AhriW.InitialDelay), since the dummy is the only enemy champion present and is therefore always the top-priority target for all three flames; its cooldown starts at that landing time, per the wiki's 'starts post-effect'. The cast itself is instant and does not hold up other casts, but it still cannot start inside one that is in progress.

Charm's damage, stated to snapshot 'at the time of its application', is taken at cast completion (0.25 s after cast start, i.e. when its cast time ends) and dealt then, since no separate travel delay is modeled elsewhere either.
Q, W and E are each recast as soon as they come off cooldown (and are not blocked by a cast in progress) for the whole fight; auto-attacks fill the remaining time between casts.
Essence Theft (P) only heals Ahri and never changes damage dealt to a stationary dummy, so it is not modeled.
Mana is not modeled: nothing here binds inside a 15 s fight at level 16.

assumed.why: the wiki gives only the 0.25 s priority-acquisition delay, not individual per-flame timing, so all three Fox-Fire flames are assumed to land together at that instant against the lone target, and the post-effect cooldown starts there.
